classification.difficultyReason: Translate two full-load cost statements into linear equations and solve using elimination.

content.prompt:
Solve this problem by introducing two pronumerals and forming a pair of simultaneous equations.

A manufacturer of lawn fertiliser produces bags of fertiliser in two sizes, standard and jumbo. To transport bags to retail outlets, he uses a van with a carrying capacity of one tonne. He discovers that he can transport either 110 standard bags and 60 jumbo bags or 50 standard bags and 100 jumbo bags at any one time. Assume that each of these loads reaches the van’s one-tonne carrying capacity. Find the weight of each type of bag.

answer.worked:
Let $s$ be the weight of a standard bag in kilograms and $j$ the weight of a jumbo bag in kilograms. Each full load weighs $1000\text{ kg}$.
$$\begin{align*}110s+60j&=1000 &&\text{(1)}\\50s+100j&=1000 &&\text{(2)}\end{align*}$$
Multiply equation (1) by 5 and equation (2) by 3:
$$\begin{align*}550s+300j&=5000 &&\text{(3)}\\150s+300j&=3000 &&\text{(4)}\end{align*}$$
Subtract equation (4) from equation (3):
$$\begin{align*}400s&=2000\\s&=5\end{align*}$$
Substitute $s=5$ into equation (2):
$$\begin{align*}50\times5+100j&=1000\\250+100j&=1000\\100j&=750\\j&=7.5\end{align*}$$
Checks:
$$\begin{align*}110\times5+60\times7.5&=1000\\50\times5+100\times7.5&=1000\end{align*}$$
A standard bag weighs $5\text{ kg}$ and a jumbo bag weighs $7.5\text{ kg}$.
